`NavigationMenu.Popup` takes its sizes in steps from `usePopupSizes` of the popup layer, and the positioner binds the size of the popup. Vue writes both styles.
The file holds the marker of the triggers for the outside press of Base UI. The popup layer takes the root element as inside, so a trigger needs no marker.
The focus-out rule of the popup layer reads the inside elements of each layer: the popup, the root element and each layer above. A part needs no check of its own.
The dismissal is the layer of the root, which listens on the document and on the root element. The list gives no handlers to the triggers.
The cases assert the `displayName` of a React context. A Vue injection key has no such name.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the root through the parts: the value with each reason, `v-model`, `cancel()`, the falsy values, `close()`, the hover with `delay` and `closeDelay`, the triangle to the popup, the patient press, the keys, the Tab order, the return of the focus, the nested roots, the content, the size steps and the placement. The parts render no transition status and no unmount action: `<Transition>` animates the popup and the backdrop, `transition` animates a content, and the hooks of `<Transition>` replace `unmount()`, `preventUnmountOnClose()` and `openChangeComplete` (rule 8.9). A triangle flag of the hover replaces the `pointer-events` styles of the safe polygon.

The cases mock the engine for a branch of the `pointer-events` styles of the safe polygon. The parts write no such style, and no code reads the engine. `NavigationMenu.test.ts` runs the triangle cases in WebKit.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the trigger: its element and attributes, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` of the content, the press, the open key of each orientation and direction, a nested trigger, `disabled` with `aria-disabled`, the hover, the activation direction, the Tab order and the size of the new content. The focus guards beside the trigger and the owner element with `aria-owns` are gone.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the content: the content of the open item in the viewport, the arrow keys, `keepMounted` in its item, in the viewport and in a kept portal, `transition` with the enter and leave classes, the close with the popup, and the scoped rule through the `element` slot. `NavigationMenu.hydration.test.ts` tests the kept content in the server HTML and after the hydration.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the list: the arrow keys of the orientation with no loop, the stop of the keys at the list, a nested list, an item that leaves, Escape, an outside press, a press in the list, a press on a trigger of another menu, and the error of a list with no root.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the link: `closeOnClick` with the reason `link-press` through each level, a link with no `closeOnClick`, no `tabindex`, a link that loses the focus with no related target, and a router link in the `element` slot with `aria-current`. `active` is cut: the developer writes `aria-current="page"`.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the positioner: its place below the trigger with insets, the side `top`, `data-instant` while the window changes its size, and the error of a positioner with no portal. The shift keeps the layout viewport as its root boundary.

`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the popup: its element, `tabindex`, the name of the shown trigger in `aria-labelledby`, a name of the developer, the `id` of the trigger, and a press on the popup with no control.
`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the portal: `keepMounted`, the target of a portal in a content, and the content in the popup of a kept portal.
`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the viewport: the content of the open item in it, and the Tab order of an inline viewport with its two sentinels.
`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the arrow: its element with `aria-hidden`, and the error of an arrow with no positioner.
`NavigationMenu.test.ts` tests the icon: its element with `aria-hidden`, the default arrow and `data-popup-open`, and the error of an icon with no item.
`NavigationMenu.test.ts` renders each item as an `<li>` element in the list.
`NavigationMenu.test.ts` renders the backdrop with `role="presentation"`.

The part reads `id` to give it to its element, or a generated id when `id` is absent, so it is a declared prop. The popup names it in `aria-labelledby` (rule 8.4).
